To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new cut angle quartz crystal with low frequency- temperature coefficients was designed and prepared.
the frequency-temperature coefficients of QCMs with new cut angles were investigated in aqueous solution, and a group of new cut angles were found to have low dF/dTs.

the cut angle of quartz crystal microbalance has a significant effect on the frequency-temperatures characteristics and the responses sensitivities to the surface mass loading and the viscodensity of a liquid phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the frequency-temperature characteristics of QCMs with new cut angles in aqueous solution, which is helpful to design a QCM sensor with low temperature coefficient in a liquid phase and to study the temperature-dependent phenomena in a liquid phase.
the frequency response characteristics of the new cut angle QCMs in aqueous phase, which is helpful to the design and fabrication of QCM-based sensors for liquid applications.
the design, fabrication and application of a new cut angle QCM with a low temperature coefficient of frequency in aqueous solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cut angle of 35.65 degrees in the yxl orientation of a 9 MHz quartz wafer is a suitable choice for a QCM in an aqueous environment.
the new cut angle QCM with low dF/d T value in an aqueous solution is an ideal sensor for the detection of mass loading or viscodensity of the solution.
a QCM with phi in the range of ca. 35.15 degrees -ca. 35.7 degrees can be applied as an intrinsically temperature compensated sensor for liquid phase measurements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new cut angle quartz crystal is an ideal sensor material in an aqueous solution for its intrinsic temperature compensation and its excellent frequency responses to surface loading and liquid properties.
the QCMs in the new cut angles have similar frequency response sensitivities to the surface mass loading and the viscodensity of the liquid.
a QCM in a new cut angle can be used to monitor the mass loading and viscosity change of a solution in a wide temperature range.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cut angle phi is an important parameter in the design of an intrinsically temperature compensated QCM.
the cut angle is an important parameter in the fabrication of QCM sensors and it can be adjusted to meet different applications.

a low frequency-temperature coefficient QCM can be obtained by choosing a proper cut angle in the range of phi=35.15- 35.7 degrees, which is a new approach for the temperature compensation of a QCM sensor in a liquid phase.
